proof:
# Two saturated facet moments force a heavy middle fiber for a strip family

This exact planar theorem excludes an entire excessive-overlap family
using actual midpoint geometry and full normal criticality. It does
not assume symmetry of the middle fiber. It is a conditional family
result, not a general OC proof.

Let L>=5, and use coordinates q=(x+y)/2, r=(x-y)/2. Put

    A_L={|q|<=L, |r|<=3/4},
    B=T={x<=1, y<=1, x+y>=-1}.

Let K be any planar convex body with 0 in int K and
(A_L+B)/2 subset K. Consider the two ambient caps x>=z and y>=z
through (0,0), for the three fibers A_L,K,B at -1,0,1. Assume each
cap has nonnegative one-sided first derivative of its captured mixed
area under every ambient normal perturbation keeping the boundary
through the source. A genuine locally minimizing cap, and hence any
globally depth-critical cap, has this property.

Then

    |K|>|A_L|+|B|=6L+9/2.                          (1)

Thus no nonheavy configuration in this family can have even these
two necessary critical-cap conditions. Equal cap masses, the third
cap's criticality, and global deepest-point optimality are not needed.

## 1. The excessive missed-mass profile and the moment equations

The coordinate change (q,r)->(x,y) has absolute determinant two, so
|A_L|=6L. The missed fractions for the three canonical caps
x>=z, y>=z, -x-y>=z are

    rho_1=rho_2=(L-1)/(2L),
    rho_3=(L-1/2)/(2L).

For example, at fixed r uniform on [-3/4,3/4], the condition x<-1
is q<-1-r. This threshold is strictly inside [-L,L]; integrating its
interval length over the symmetric r range proves rho_1. The others
follow identically. Their sum is

    kappa=3/2-5/(4L)>=5/4,

with strict excess when L>5.

The A_L section at x=-1 is y in [-5/2,1/2], so its length is three
and its centroid is (-1,-1). The B supporting edge x=1 also has
length three, with centroid (1,-1/2). For the middle x=0 chord write
its endpoints as (0,-q_1),(0,p_1), where p_1,q_1>0. Its length is
t_1=p_1+q_1 and its centroid coordinate is c_1=(p_1-q_1)/2.

The equal endpoint section masses force the entire B facet to enter
the first-order balance. This can be checked without an allocation
compactness argument. For a tangent normal perturbation w and an
integer tilt perturbation beta, choose beta so large that wy+beta
is positive on the whole B edge. The proper A and K section
derivatives and the supporting-edge derivative then sum to

    w[-3+t_1*c_1-3/2],

because the beta coefficients -3 and +3 cancel. This must be
nonnegative for both signs of w. Consequently t_1*c_1=9/2, or

    p_1^2-q_1^2=9.                                  (2)

The symmetric endpoint geometry, without any symmetry assumption on
K, gives for the y=0 chord endpoints (-q_2,0),(p_2,0)

    p_2^2-q_2^2=9.                                  (3)

In particular p_1,p_2>3. All sections here are actual sections of
one body at the stated cuts; no free centroids have been assigned.

## 2. Shared midpoint points couple the two chord equations

Define

    U=(4L+11)/8, V=(4L-7)/8,
    W=(4L+7)/8,  J=(4L+1)/8.

Actual midpoint compatibility places each of the following four
points in K:

    (-U,-V), (-V,-U), (W,J), (J,W).                 (4)

They are vertex midpoints of A_L and B. In particular the segment
from (-V,-U) to (p_2,0) crosses x=0 at
(0,-U*p_2/(V+p_2)). Similarly for the other axis. Hence

    q_1>=U*p_2/(V+p_2),
    q_2>=U*p_1/(V+p_1).                            (5)

Set p=min(p_1,p_2). If p=p_1, the first inequality, the increasing
function t->Ut/(V+t), and (2) imply

    sqrt(p^2-9)>=U*p/(V+p).                        (6)

The other case is identical. Notice that using only the separate
chord-ratio bound would discard precisely this coupling through
the same southwest midpoint points.

## 3. An exact area threshold incompatible with the chord moments

Set

    p_H=[(9/2)L+57/16]/(L+3/2).

For L>=5, elementary subtraction gives

    p_H-3=3(8L-5)/[8(2L+3)]>0,
    L+1-p_H=(4L-11)(4L+3)/[8(2L+3)]>0.             (7)

At p=p_H, squaring the nonnegative sides in (6) gives the test

    E=(p_H^2-9)(V+p_H)^2-U^2*p_H^2.

Exact expansion yields

    E=-9 P(L)/[4096(2L+3)^4],

where

    P(L)=16384L^6+4096L^5-410624L^4+864192L^3
                    +3318576L^2+2700228L+671769.

This polynomial is strictly positive for every L>=5. Indeed for
t=L-5>=0 its exact expansion is

    P(t+5)=16384t^6+495616t^5+5835776t^4+34635712t^3
                     +113407856t^2+215388388t+217321309.

Every coefficient is positive. Therefore (6) fails at p_H. Moreover
sqrt(1-9/p^2) increases for p>=3 while U/(V+p) decreases. Dividing
(6) by p shows that it fails for every p<=p_H as well. Hence the
actual chord endpoints necessarily satisfy

    min(p_1,p_2)>p_H.                              (8)

Choose any p_0 with

    p_H<p_0<min(p_1,p_2,L+1),

which exists by (7) and (8). Since 0 belongs to K, the points
(p_0,0),(0,p_0) lie on the actual source chords and belong to K.
Together with (4), their convex hull is the hexagon in cyclic order

    (-U,-V), (-V,-U), (p_0,0),
                         (W,J), (J,W), (0,p_0).

Its consecutive turn determinants, in symmetric pairs, are

    9(2L+2p_0+1)/8,
    (16L p_0-24L+24p_0-21)/16,
    3(L+1-p_0)/4.

All are strictly positive: p_0>3 and L>=5 handle the middle one,
and the remaining ones are immediate. Thus this is an actual convex
hexagon contained in K. Its shoelace area is

    (L+3/2)p_0+(3/2)L+15/16.

At p_0=p_H this expression is exactly 6L+9/2. Since p_0>p_H,
the contained hexagon already has area greater than |A_L|+|B|.
This proves (1).

## 4. What this charge establishes and what it does not

The mixed-area lower bound from the unaugmented midpoint body alone
need not make K heavy for these strips. The additional area comes
from the positive source-chord endpoints forced by exact facet-moment
balance. Convexity then couples those endpoints to the SAME negative
midpoint points and charges a single contained polygon to |K|.

The proof covers a continuum L>=5 and every compatible K, including
asymmetric and nonsmooth ones. It uses no halfspace orientation
restriction in the criticality assumption: full ambient variations
are what force (2) and (3). It does not prove that all excessive-overlap
families admit this same polygon charge, and it does not convert a
moment-body centroid condition into higher-dimensional section
containment.
